newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle market standstill -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle market standstill -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were at a standstill near midday Tuesday as packer buyers and cattle owners continued their standoff, feedlot sources said.
Light bids at $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt were passed by owners seeking $68.00 to $69.00, they said.
Several feedlot managers were optimistic that fed cattle prices this week would be underpinned by firm beef values and outlooks for strong retail beef demand, the sources said.
Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.20 to $0.47 per cwt, with 178 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
Heavyweight choice beef at midday was quoted up $0.20 at $105.33, up $0.78 since Friday, USDA statistics showed. Heavier-weight choice beef slid $1.75 last week.

Feedlot conditions in the Texas Panhandle reportedly were improving amid sunny skies and temperatures in the 70s Fahrenheit. Feedyards Friday and Saturday were soaked by heavy rainfall and deep snow, which left them sloppy.

Showlists this week were estimated near 92,000 head in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, down 6,000 from last week. The showlist in Kansas was pegged near 85,000 head, up 5,000, market sources said.
